forms: pick the example of a talent
tell an ability from an interest
pick a way to grow a talent
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.SOCIAL.SELF_EXPLORATION.SE_ABILI.mastery: The child tells an ability (what a person can do), a talent (a natural gift), an interest (what a person likes to do) and a skill (what is learnt by practice), and picks practice, feedback and joining clubs as ways to grow them. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the personal value
say what a value is
say what a person with steady values does under pressure
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.SOCIAL.SELF_EXPLORATION.SE_VALUE.mastery: The child says a personal value is a belief about what is right that guides how a person acts (honesty, respect, responsibility, perseverance, kindness, integrity), tells values from possessions, and says a steady person keeps their values when friends pressure them to do wrong. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the feeling from a short story
pick a healthy way to handle the feeling
say what a harmful way is
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.SOCIAL.SELF_EXPLORATION.SE_EMOTI.mastery: The child names feelings (happiness, love, fear, anger, sadness) from a story and picks healthy ways to manage them (breathing slowly, pausing before speaking, talking to a trusted adult, exercise, writing it down) over harmful ones (shouting, hitting, hiding it for ever, revenge). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match a learner to a suitable opportunity
say what a business idea needs to start
say what a social entrepreneur does
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.SOCIAL.ENTREPRENEURIAL_OPPORTUN..mastery: The child matches a described personality or talent to a sensible opportunity, and says a social entrepreneur solves a community problem through an enterprise, and that a start needs a need people have, a plan, some capital, skills, honesty and a customer. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which story belongs to which community
say who the first man and woman are in a story
say who the creator is in a story
say how such stories were passed on
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.HUMAN_ORIGIN.HO_TRADITION.mastery: The child tells that African communities hold their own stories of how people began, for example the Agikuyu story of Gikuyu and Mumbi under the Mukuru wa Gathanga tree given by Ngai, and the Maasai story that Enkai sent down cattle; that they were told aloud by elders; and that each community values its own. Stories are marked for a teacher or resource person to confirm. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say who the first man and woman are
say what a religious story and a traditional story both teach
pick the common aspect
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.HUMAN_ORIGIN.HO_RELIGIOUS.mastery: The child tells that the Christian story names Adam and Eve made by God in the garden of Eden (Genesis), the Islamic story names Adam and Hawa made by Allah, and picks the common aspects of religious and traditional stories: a creator, a first man and a first woman, a special place, and the idea that people have a purpose and must be respected. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which factor helped which kingdom
pick the main reason a kingdom grew
say which kingdom is famous for what
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.EARLY_CIVILISATION.EC_FAC.mastery: The child says ancient Egypt grew on the fertile Nile valley with yearly floods and farming, Great Zimbabwe on cattle, gold and long-distance trade with the coast (its stone walls), and the Kingdom of Kongo on the fertile Congo River area, farming, iron and copper working and trade with strong central rule under the Manikongo. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which part of Africa a kingdom was in
say which river or sea it was near
say which modern country holds its remains
read a small table of kingdoms and places
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.EARLY_CIVILISATION.EC_LOC.mastery: The child places ancient Egypt in the north-east of Africa along the River Nile, Great Zimbabwe in southern Africa between the Limpopo and Zambezi rivers (today in Zimbabwe), and the Kingdom of Kongo in west-central Africa near the mouth of the Congo River (today parts of Angola and the two Congos). Map questions are in words or a small described table. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what an ancient kingdom gave the world
say which kingdom gave which idea
say why it still matters today
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.EARLY_CIVILISATION.EC_CON.mastery: The child says Egypt gave writing (hieroglyphs), papyrus paper, a 365-day calendar, geometry for building, medicine and the pyramids; Great Zimbabwe gave stone building without mortar and a model of trade and gold working; Kongo gave skilled copper and iron work, cloth and its system of government and trade; and that these ideas still influence the world. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the form of servitude described
say how a form differs from another
say which is slavery today
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.SLAVERY_AND_SERVITUDE.SL_.mastery: The child tells slavery (a person owned and forced to work), domestic servitude, debt bondage or pledging, serfdom and indenture in the past, and child labour, forced labour, trafficking and forced marriage today, and says each takes away a person's freedom and dignity. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say why people were traded
say who bought and who sold
say what made the trade grow
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.SLAVERY_AND_SERVITUDE.SL_.mastery: The child says the trade grew because of demand for workers on plantations (cloves in Zanzibar, sugar on the islands), in homes and ports of Arabia and the Gulf, because ivory and slaves were carried together along trade routes, because monsoon winds carried dhows, and because Zanzibar became a trading centre. Coastal and inland leaders also took part. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which African coast was involved
say where people were taken to
say which island was a centre
read a small table of regions
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.SLAVERY_AND_SERVITUDE.SL_.mastery: The child says the trade reached from Ethiopia and the Horn and the East African coast (Kilwa, Zanzibar, Mombasa, Mozambique) inland as far as Lake Victoria and the Congo basin, and carried people to Arabia, the Persian Gulf, India and islands such as Zanzibar and Réunion. Map questions are in words or a small described table. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what barter is
say a problem of barter
say how money fixes it
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.DEVELOPMENTS_IN_MEDIUM_O..mastery: The child says barter is swapping goods for goods with no money, that it needs both people to want what the other has, that goods are hard to divide, store and carry or to value, and that money gives a common measure of value, is easy to carry and store and is accepted by all. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what was used before coins
say what led to money
say what money changed
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.DEVELOPMENTS_IN_MEDIUM_O..mastery: The child says people used cowrie shells, beads, salt, iron hoes, cattle and gold before coins; that growth of long-distance trade, towns and colonial rule (rupees and later the East African shilling) led to coins and notes; and that money made trade easier, brought wages and taxes, helped banks and savings, but also debt and a gap between rich and poor. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a factor of diversity
say which differences a person chooses and which not
say why diversity is not a problem
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.DIVERSITY_AND_INTERPERSO..mastery: The child names age, gender, ethnic group, religion, race, language, ability or disability, family background, talents and interests as what makes people different, and says differences enrich society and are not a reason to treat anyone unfairly. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the skill from a story
pick a desirable attribute
pick an undesirable attribute
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.DIVERSITY_AND_INTERPERSO..mastery: The child pairs effective communication, negotiation, assertiveness and empathy with a short story, and sorts honesty, respect, kindness, humility, responsibility and tolerance as desirable and bullying, jealousy, gossip, arrogance and dishonesty as undesirable. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a quality of a peaceful person
pick an action of a peaceful person
say what a peaceful person avoids
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.PEACEFUL_COEXISTENCE.PE_Q.mastery: The child names tolerance, forgiveness, respect, honesty, fairness, patience, kindness and willingness to listen as qualities of a peaceful person, and says a peaceful person avoids revenge, insults and spreading rumours. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a factor that promotes peace
pick a factor that breaks peace
say who helps keep peace in the community
say why peace matters
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.PEACEFUL_COEXISTENCE.PE_F.mastery: The child picks respect for the law, justice and fairness, equal sharing of resources, dialogue, religious and cultural tolerance, good leaders, peace committees and elders as factors that promote peace, and says peace lets people farm, trade, study and be safe. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say the first step to take
say what a mediator does
pick the method for a story
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.PEOPLE.PEACEFUL_COEXISTENCE.PE_R.mastery: The child puts the steps in order (stay calm, listen to each side, name the problem, suggest solutions, agree and keep the agreement) and picks negotiation, mediation, arbitration or reconciliation by what each does, and says violence is not a method. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what community service learning is
say what a CSL project is
say what a community need is
say how CSL helps
SOCI.G7.COMMUN.COMMUNITY_SERVICE_LEARNI..mastery: The child says community service learning (CSL) is learning by serving a community need, a CSL project is a planned activity that meets a real need, a community need is a gap such as litter or a bare school compound, and that CSL builds skills and values, solves real problems and strengthens the bond between the school and the community. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say the first step
put two steps in order
say what a plan holds
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.COMMUN.COMMUNITY_SERVICE_LEARNI..mastery: The child puts the steps in order: identify a need, plan (who, what, when, resources), carry out the activity, report and reflect on it, and says a good plan names tasks, people, time and resources. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the source from a description
say which source is oral
say which is archaeological
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.HISTORICAL_INFORMATION.HI.mastery: The child names oral traditions, written records, archaeology (artefacts, fossils, buildings), language (linguistics), genealogies, photographs and audio-visual records, and ethnography as sources, and matches each to an example. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say whether a source is primary or secondary
pick the primary source
pick the secondary source
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.HISTORICAL_INFORMATION.HI.mastery: The child says a primary source was made at the time by someone who was there (a diary, a letter, an old photograph, a treaty, a tool) and a secondary source was written later by someone who was not (a textbook, an encyclopaedia, a documentary), and sorts examples correctly. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say how oral history was kept
say how written records are kept
say how objects and sites are kept
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.HISTORICAL_INFORMATION.HI.mastery: The child says oral history was kept in songs, proverbs, riddles and stories told by elders and now recorded on audio and video; writing on papyrus, paper and now digital files; objects in museums and archives; and sites by law and by the National Museums of Kenya. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which region grew which crop
say which factor favoured farming
say which animals were reared
say what domestication is
SOCI.G7.NATURA.HISTORICAL_DEVELOPMENT_O..mastery: The child says early farming in Africa began in the Nile Valley (wheat, barley, flax), the Ethiopian highlands (teff, coffee) and the West African savanna and Sahel (sorghum, millet, African rice, yams), that animals reared were cattle, sheep, goats and donkeys, and picks fertile soil, reliable water, a suitable climate and wild plants and animals to tame as the factors. Domestication means taming wild plants and animals. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what the yearly flood gave
say what irrigation is
say what a food surplus allowed
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.HISTORICAL_DEVELOPMENT_O..mastery: The child says the yearly Nile flood left rich silt, that irrigation (canals and the shaduf) carried water to fields, that a food surplus let some people become scribes, priests, builders and traders, and that this led to writing, a calendar, record keeping, towns and government. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what lines cross Africa
say which oceans and seas border it
say its size
say its shape
SOCI.G7.NATURA.MAPS_AND_MAP_WORK.MM_AFRI.mastery: The child says Africa is the second largest continent (about 30 million square kilometres), the equator crosses its middle so most of it lies in the tropics, the Tropic of Cancer crosses the north and the Tropic of Capricorn the south, the Atlantic Ocean lies to the west, the Indian Ocean to the east, the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Red Sea to the north-east, and the shape is wide in the north and narrows to the south. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say north or south from a latitude
say east or west from a longitude
pick the place from its position
read a small table of places
SOCI.G7.NATURA.MAPS_AND_MAP_WORK.MM_LATL.mastery: The child reads a latitude (degrees north or south of the equator) first and then a longitude (degrees east or west of the Prime Meridian), says whether a place is in the northern or southern hemisphere and east or west of the Prime Meridian, and picks the place from a small table. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: work out the time in an eastern place
work out the time in a western place
work out the time difference between two longitudes
say how many degrees make an hour
SOCI.G7.NATURA.MAPS_AND_MAP_WORK.MM_TIME.mastery: The child says the earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours so 15 degrees is one hour and 1 degree is 4 minutes, that places east of Greenwich are ahead and places west are behind, and works out the local time or the time difference from the longitudes, adding in the east and subtracting in the west. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which feature is largest, longest or highest
say where a feature is
say which countries share a feature
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.MAPS_AND_MAP_WORK.MM_FEAT.mastery: The child says the Nile is the longest river and flows north to the Mediterranean, the Sahara is the largest hot desert, Mount Kilimanjaro (Tanzania) is the highest mountain, Lake Victoria is the largest lake and is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, the Congo Basin holds a great rain forest, the Kalahari and Namib deserts lie in the south-west, and the Atlas Mountains lie in the north-west. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which planet the earth is from the Sun
say the shape of the earth
pick the evidence that the earth is round
say what the big bang theory says
SOCI.G7.NATURA.EARTH_AND_THE_SOLAR_SYST..mastery: The child says the earth is about 4.5 billion years old and formed from a cloud of gas and dust around the young Sun (the nebula idea; the big bang theory is for the universe), is the third planet from the Sun of eight, is almost a sphere about 12,700 kilometres across, and picks evidence such as ships disappearing hull first, the round shadow in a lunar eclipse and photographs from space. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what causes day and night
say what causes the seasons
say how long a rotation and a revolution take
say why the time differs between places
SOCI.G7.NATURA.EARTH_AND_THE_SOLAR_SYST..mastery: The child says rotation is the earth spinning on its axis once in 24 hours, causing day and night and differences in time between places; revolution is the earth going round the Sun once in about 365 and a quarter days, giving a leap year every four years; and the tilt of the axis (about 23.5 degrees) with revolution gives the seasons away from the equator. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the layer from its description
put the layers in order from the top
say which layer is liquid
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.EARTH_AND_THE_SOLAR_SYST..mastery: The child names the crust (thin, solid, outermost), the mantle (thick, hot, with molten rock called magma at the top), the outer core (liquid iron and nickel) and the inner core (solid, hottest), in order from the surface, and says the crust is the thinnest layer and we live on it. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the instrument for an element
pick the element an instrument measures
say what a Stevenson screen is for
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.WEATHER.WE_ELEMENTS.mastery: The child names temperature (thermometer), rainfall (rain gauge), humidity (hygrometer), air pressure (barometer), wind direction (wind vane), wind speed (anemometer), sunshine (sunshine recorder) and cloud cover, says a Stevenson screen shelters the instruments from rain and direct sun, and tells weather (short term) from climate (long term). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say how weather affects an activity
pick the right response to a weather warning
say what a forecast helps with
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.WEATHER.WE_SIGNIFICANCE.mastery: The child says weather affects farming (planting and harvest), transport, building, clothing, health and safety, that forecasts help people plan, and picks safe responses (stay indoors and away from trees in lightning, avoid crossing flooded rivers, drink water and cover up in great heat, take shelter in a storm). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the method for a task
say what a questionnaire is
say what an interview is
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.FIELDWORK.FW_METHODS.mastery: The child names observation, questionnaires, interviews, focus group discussions and measuring or counting, and picks the best method for a task (counting vehicles by observation, asking a driver by interview, many written questions by questionnaire). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the solution to a challenge
say the safe thing to do on a road
say why permission is needed
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.NATURA.FIELDWORK.FW_CHALLENGES.mastery: The child pairs bad weather, cost, shortage of time, unwilling respondents, getting lost and road danger with their solutions (check the forecast, a small budget, a timetable, explaining the purpose politely, a map and a guide, crossing at a safe place with a teacher), and says to get permission first. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

pick a graph for the data
SOCI.G7.NATURA.FIELDWORK.FW_ANALYSIS.mastery: The child works out the mean (total divided by the number of values), the median (the middle value when ordered) and the mode (the value that occurs most) for a small set of whole numbers, and picks a table, bar graph or pie chart to show data. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

SOCI.G7.POLITI.POLITICAL_DEVELOPMENT_IN..mastery: The child says explorers mapped routes and reported on resources, missionaries opened mission stations, schools and hospitals and prepared the way, traders and chartered companies (for example the Imperial British East Africa Company) set up trade and signed treaties, and colonial officers and armies took control; and gives raw materials, markets, strategic places and national pride as reasons. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

SOCI.G7.POLITI.POLITICAL_DEVELOPMENT_IN..mastery: The child says European powers (and the United States as an observer) met in Berlin in 1884 to 1885, hosted by Chancellor Bismarck of Germany, no African leaders were present, and its terms were that a power must occupy a region effectively to claim it, must tell the others of a claim, and that the Congo and Niger rivers be open to trade; it set the rules for the scramble and borders were drawn later. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G7.POLITI.POLITICAL_DEVELOPMENT_IN..mastery: The child says colonial rule took away independence and land, drew borders that split some communities and joined others, brought taxes, forced labour and cash crops for European industry, harmed local culture, and also brought roads, railways, schools and new languages that served the colonial interest. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

SOCI.G7.POLITI.POLITICAL_DEVELOPMENT_IN..mastery: The child says neo-colonialism is when a powerful country still controls a free one through trade, debt, money and politics, and picks accountability, honesty, fair elections, the rule of law, building local industry and using resources for the people as good governance that reduces it. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

SOCI.G7.POLITI.THE_CONSTITUTION_OF_KENY..mastery: The child says the Constitution is the supreme law of Kenya, was promulgated on 27 August 2010, sets out the rights of every person in the Bill of Rights, how the government is organised, the national values and how power is shared with the counties, and that every person and leader must obey it. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

SOCI.G7.POLITI.THE_CONSTITUTION_OF_KENY..mastery: The child picks learning the Constitution, obeying the law, voting, taking part in public meetings, paying taxes, respecting the rights of others and reporting corruption as ways to uphold it, and rejects bribery, hate speech and ignoring court orders. SOCI.G7.POLITI.THE_CONSTITUTION_OF_KENY..mastery: The child names the national values and principles of governance in Article 10: patriotism, national unity, sharing and devolution of power, the rule of law, democracy and participation of the people, human dignity, equity, social justice, inclusiveness, equality, human rights, non-discrimination, good governance, integrity, transparency, accountability and sustainable development, and matches a value to an action. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

SOCI.G7.POLITI.HUMAN_RIGHTS.HR_EQUITY.mastery: The child says human rights are universal (for all), inalienable (cannot be taken away), indivisible and equal, tells equality (everyone gets the same) from equity (everyone gets what is fair for their need), and says discrimination is unfair treatment because of who a person is. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
